chunks: From him, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a house in which silver coins are found, so he said: 'If it is inhabited and its people are in it, then it belongs to them. And if it is ruined and its people have left it, then the one who found the money is more entitled to it.'
ai.seo_question: Who owns found money discovered in an inhabited versus an abandoned house according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* to distinguish between property rights in occupied versus abandoned dwellings, a key principle in Shia jurisprudence regarding *luqata* (found items). The hadith clarifies that possession is determined by the presence of inhabitants rather than mere ownership, ensuring that the finder of silver (*wariq*) in an empty house has a stronger claim than the absent owner.
